title: Eleven Elections
subject: Two poll clerks share a trestle table in a village hall only on election days, eleven in twenty years, until she catches herself hoping for a snap election and, as the box is sealed at ten, he asks why wait for the next.
caption: Salsa, classic New York salsa dura style with a live orchestra feel. Piano playing a syncopated montuno in octaves, two trumpets and two trombones on punchy unison riffs and mambo breaks, baby bass on a rolling tumbao, congas with timbales and cowbell locked to a 2-3 clave, güiro scraping eighth notes. Live room recording, warm analog horns. Female mezzo-soprano, bright full chest voice, three-voice coro answering the refrain. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 92 BPM, E-flat major. Warm, hopeful, wry. No electronic beats, no reggaeton dembow, no autotune, no rap, no synth pads, no distorted guitars.
lyrics:
[Intro - piano montuno, congas, horn hit]

[Verse 1]
Trestle table in the village hall
Pencils on strings and a flask of tea
Eleven elections in twenty years
You across the table from me

[Pre-Chorus]
I read the news and I caught myself
Hoping they'd call another one

[Chorus]
Eleven elections, I counted every one
Eleven elections, and the polls are almost done
Why wait, why wait, why wait for the next
Why wait for the next one, come on

[Verse 2]
Ten o'clock, we seal the box
You turn the key and you clear your throat
You say it quiet, over the wax
And you pass me a pencil with a note

[Pre-Chorus]
I read it twice and I read it slow
It says, why wait for another one

[Chorus]
Eleven elections, and I'll keep this one
Eleven elections, and the counting's done
Why wait, why wait, no, don't wait for the next
Dance with me now, come on

[Outro - mambo horns, congas, piano]
Why wait, why wait for the next
